note: Ps109 imprecatory psalm (31v, ~137 spans). Read by CHAR-ARC. A enemies' assault v1-5 (WICKED/DECEITFUL/LYING mouths, HATE/HATRED, accusing in return for the psalmist's LOVE/GOOD/PRAYER; they reward EVIL for good); B imprecation + the wicked's character v6-20 (WICKED-MAN/ACCUSER, GUILTY/SIN; because he did not REMEMBER to show KINDNESS/PITY but PURSUED the POOR/NEEDY/BROKENHEARTED, LOVED to CURSE, no DELIGHT in blessing); C affliction v22-25 (POOR/NEEDY, HEART stricken, KNEES weak, BODY gaunt, SCORN); D plea->thanks v27-31 (KNOW it's your hand, let them CURSE but you bless, PUT-TO-SHAME/GLAD, ACCUSERS' DISHONOR/SHAME, THANKS/PRAISE, the NEEDY-ONE's SOUL saved). God's deal/steadfast-love/deliver/help/save/bless/stands = qualifiers; mouths/tongues/garment/locust imagery = standalone.

dims.v: paired with the plea that God not be silent
v1: 'Be not silent, O God of my PRAISE (tehillah)!' - the psalmist's worship, the God he praises now begged not to stay silent against his slanderers.
paired with deceitful and lying mouths
v2: 'For WICKED (rasha) and deceitful mouths are opened against me' - the godless foes whose mouths assail him.
paired with the wicked and lying mouths
v2: 'wicked and DECEITFUL (mirmah) mouths are opened against me' - the treachery of the enemies' speech.
v2: 'speaking against me with LYING (sheqer) tongues' - the falsehood of the foes' accusations.
v3: 'They encircle me with words of HATE (sinah)' - the enmity that surrounds him, hatred without cause.
paired with the accusation returned for it
v4: 'In return for my LOVE (ahabah) they accuse me' - the psalmist's goodwill met with accusation, love repaid with enmity.
paired with the love they repay
v4: 'they ACCUSE (satan) me' - the enemies' adversarial attack, standing against him as accusers.
paired with the love returned with accusation
v4: 'but I give myself to PRAYER (tephillah)' - the psalmist's response to hostility: not retaliation but prayer, love answered by devotion to God.
v5: 'So they reward me EVIL (ra) for good' - the enemies' return of evil for the psalmist's good.
v5: 'they reward me evil for GOOD (tob)' - the psalmist's good, met with evil.
v5: 'and HATRED (sinah) for my love' - the enemies' hatred returned for the psalmist's love.
v5: 'and hatred for my LOVE (ahabah)' - the psalmist's love, answered with hatred.
paired with the accuser at his right hand
v6: 'Appoint a WICKED MAN (rasha) against him' - the imprecation's opening: a wicked adversary invoked over the enemy.
v6: 'let an ACCUSER (satan) stand at his right hand' - the adversary invoked to accuse the enemy as he accused the psalmist.
paired with his prayer counted as sin
v7: 'When he is tried, let him come forth GUILTY (rasha)' - the wish that the enemy be condemned at judgment.
v7: 'let his prayer be counted as SIN (chataah)' - the wish that even the enemy's prayer be reckoned guilt.
paired with the widow and the curse
v9: 'May his children be FATHERLESS (yathom)' - the imprecation reaching the enemy's children, bereaved by his fall.
paired with none to pity his children
v12: 'Let there be none to extend KINDNESS (chesed) to him' - the wish that the merciless man find no mercy.
v12: 'nor any to PITY (chanan) his fatherless children' - the wish that the pitiless find no pity for his own.
v14: 'May the INIQUITY (avon) of his fathers be remembered by the LORD' - the ancestral guilt invoked against the enemy.
v14: 'and let not the SIN (chattath) of his mother be blotted out' - the invoked guilt of the enemy's mother.
v16: 'For he did not REMEMBER (zakar) to show kindness' - the ground of the whole curse: the enemy's forgetting of mercy.
paired with the failure to remember
v16: 'did not remember to show KINDNESS (chesed)' - the mercy the enemy withheld, the root of his condemnation.
the poor and needy to death
paired with the poor, needy, brokenhearted
v16: 'but PURSUED (radaph) the poor and needy and brokenhearted, to death' - the enemy's cruel persecution of the afflicted.
paired with the needy and brokenhearted
v16: 'pursued the POOR (ani)' - the afflicted victim the enemy hounded.
v16: 'the poor and NEEDY (ebyon)' - the destitute the enemy persecuted.
paired with the poor and needy
v16: 'and the BROKENHEARTED (kaah), to death' - the crushed in spirit the enemy hounded to the grave.
paired with cursing and the absence of delight in blessing
v17: 'He LOVED (aheb) to curse; let curses come upon him!' - the enemy's delight in cursing, now recoiling on him.
v17: 'He loved to CURSE (qelalah)' - the cursing the enemy delighted in.
v17: 'he did not DELIGHT (chaphets) in blessing; may it be far from him!' - the enemy's aversion to blessing, blessing now kept far from him.
v18: 'He clothed himself with CURSING (qelalah) as his coat' - cursing worn like a garment, soaked into his very being.
paired with speaking evil against his life
v20: 'May this be the reward of my ACCUSERS (satan) from the LORD' - the adversaries whose recompense the imprecation seeks.
v20: 'of those who speak EVIL (ra) against my life' - the malice of the accusers' speech.
paired with being needy and the stricken heart
v22: 'For I am POOR (ani) and needy' - the psalmist's lowliness, his plea's ground, set against his powerful foes.
v22: 'For I am poor and NEEDY (ebyon)' - the destitution the psalmist pleads.
paired with the poverty and the wasting body
v22: 'and my HEART (leb) is stricken within me' - the wounded inner self, grief pierced deep.
v24: 'My KNEES (berek) are weak through fasting' - the body failing under grief, strength drained from the very legs.
v24: 'my BODY (basar) has become gaunt' - the flesh wasted by affliction, the toll of grief made visible.
v24: 'my body has BECOME GAUNT (kachash)' - the leanness of the fasting sufferer, wasted with sorrow.
v25: 'I am an object of SCORN (cherpah) to my accusers' - the psalmist's humiliation, mocked by his foes who wag their heads.
v27: 'Let them KNOW (yada) that this is your hand' - the wish that the foes recognize God's deliverance, vindication made plain.
paired with God's blessing that overrules it
v28: 'Let them CURSE (qalal), but you will bless!' - the enemies' cursing, powerless against God's blessing.
v28: 'They arise and are PUT TO SHAME (bosh), but your servant will be glad!' - the foes shamed, the servant gladdened.
paired with the enemies put to shame
v28: 'but your servant will be GLAD (samach)!' - the joy of the vindicated servant, gladness answering the curse.
v29: 'May my ACCUSERS (satan) be clothed with dishonour' - the adversaries invoked to wear their own disgrace.
paired with the accusers and shame
v29: 'be clothed with DISHONOUR (kelimmah)' - the disgrace invoked on the accusers, worn like a garment.
v29: 'and wrapped in their own SHAME (bosheth) as in a cloak' - the shame that covers the accusers, their own disgrace their clothing.
paired with praising in the throng
v30: 'With my mouth I will give great THANKS (yadah) to the LORD' - the vow of thanksgiving, the lament turning to praise.
v30: 'I will PRAISE (halal) him in the midst of the throng' - the public praise of the delivered.
by God at his right hand
v31: 'For he stands at the right hand of the NEEDY ONE (ebyon)' - the poor whom God defends, standing where the accuser stood (v6).
v31: 'to save him from those who condemn his SOUL (nephesh)' - the life of the needy God rescues from his judges.
